revenue_share_company_owned_fy2025.rationale: Secondary source; flagged wherever shown. GROUP-WIDE: global context only, never applied to Singapore (Singapore is company-owned, I-sg-owned).

sg_outlets_press_range.unit: outlets in Singapore, as press reports vary
sg_outlets_press_range.rationale: Speaker notes only. Press counts of Singapore outlets vary between these values; the slide keeps sg_outlets (store directory, October 2026).

registered_members_jun2026.unit: registered members, group-wide, end of June 2026
registered_members_jun2026.rationale: Company statement on the Q2 2026 earnings call (COO, interpreted). Group-wide, not Singapore. Membership is on Chagee's mobile mini program (L-chagee-q1-2025).

repeat_member_order_share.unit: share of total orders from members who made 2 or more purchases (stated as 'more than'), Q2 2026
repeat_member_order_share.rationale: Company statement on the Q2 2026 earnings call. A floor ('more than 78%'). Group-wide, not Singapore.

signal_strength_default.unit: share, 0 = no pre-launch signal, 1 = strong signal
signal_strength_default.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Slide 2 slider default. Band half-width u = uncertainty_no_signal - signal x (uncertainty_no_signal - uncertainty_strong_signal), a straight line between the two approved end points. At 0.5, u = 32.5%. This u feeds slides 3 and 5.

remove_hype_default.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Slide 2 starts with opening-week hype removed, so slides 3-5 receive the steady-demand band by default. The hype band stays visible on the chart for comparison.

open_hours_per_day.rationale: Generic mall/high-street trading day (10:00-22:00). Structural: sets the length of the simulated day.

open_days_per_year.rationale: Allows for a few closure days. Only converts cups/year to cups/day.

cups_per_store_per_year.rationale: About 555 cups/day after the opening period. No public per-store cup figure in the ledger; GMV per store cannot be turned into cups without an average ticket price, which the ledger does not have. Wide range on purpose.

hourly_demand_share.unit: share of daily cups per open hour (10:00 to 22:00), sums to 1
hourly_demand_share.rationale: Lunch peak and an evening plateau, typical of a tea shop. Peak hour = 11% of the day. Structural; the surge setting tests peaks above it.

uncertainty_definition.rationale: Uncertainty u = (high - low) / 2 / base, as a % of the forecast base. This is exactly the band width that slide 2 outputs, and it is the x-axis of the slide 4 crossover chart.

band_coverage.rationale: The low-high band is an 80% interval: true demand = base x (1 + u x z / 1.2816), z standard normal. So 1 in 10 stores lands above high and 1 in 10 below low. An 80% band is a common planning interval; a 95% band would make the same u mean less spread.

demand_floor_share_of_base.rationale: Demand draws are floored at zero (user change; was 0.20). A draw can be a store with no demand. At u = 0.60, P(z < -2.14) is about 1.6% of draws.

uncertainty_no_signal.rationale: Slide 2: band before any pre-launch app signal, i.e. a judgement-led forecast in a new market. Illustrative.

uncertainty_strong_signal.rationale: Slide 2: band with a strong pre-launch waitlist signal. It does not reach zero because tourist and non-app demand stay invisible (named blind spot).

opening_hype_multiplier.rationale: Slide 2 toggle 'remove opening-week hype'. Sanity check only: L-gabgrowth reports 1,000+ cups on the KL opening day, about 1.8x our 555/day base, but that is one day, one store, from a secondary source.

opening_hype_weeks.rationale: How long the hype lasts before demand settles. Illustrative.

uncertainty_sweep.rationale: x-axis of the crossover chart. Covers strong-signal to no-signal bands from slide 2.

surge_multiplier.rationale: Slide 4 toggle. Applied to the two busiest hours. Default = moderate. The counter is sized to the forecast curve without the surge, so a surge is the unplanned peak that piles up behind fixed capacity.

surge_hours.unit: busiest forecast hours that get the surge
surge_hours.rationale: This number was only in the surge_multiplier rationale; it now has its own field so the code reads it from here. With the default curve these are 12:00-14:00 (ties go to the earlier hour).

surge_default.rationale: Default toggle position and printed state.

human_seconds_per_cup.unit: seconds of one average worker per cup
human_seconds_per_cup.rationale: Totals 60 s, so one average worker makes about 1 cup/min. Range is a multiplier on all six. Stylised benchmark: Chagee already uses QR-scan dispensing (L-unsw), so 'all-human' is a reference case, not Chagee's current counter.

machine_seconds_per_cup.unit: seconds per cup per machine unit
machine_seconds_per_cup.rationale: Topping/finish is the hardest step to automate, so it is the slowest machine (4 cups/min per unit). Range is a multiplier on all six. The high end, 2.0, puts the slowest station at 30 s (2 cups/min per unit), as the user asked; was 1.3. No public per-station machine times; Gong cha's company-reported productivity figures are not per station, so they are not used.

mixed_machine_stations.rationale: Fixed-time steps go to machines; cup/ice, topping/finish and handover (more variable) stay with people, who share the work including one flexible worker.

machine_speed_variation_cv.rationale: Machines run at a fixed speed (brief.md section 2). Machine breakdowns are not modelled; this flatters automation, and the slide will say so.

human_speed_variation_cv.unit: coefficient of variation, minute to minute
human_speed_variation_cv.rationale: Random minute-to-minute variation in a worker's pace.

worker_speed_spread.rationale: Workers differ in speed (slowest 0.8x, fastest 1.2x by default). This is what the bucket brigade rebalances.

coordination_loss_human.rationale: Pooling assumes perfect rebalancing. Handovers, walking and bumping at a small counter lose some of that. The Week 5 engine at realistic walk-back speed gives an information-only calibration point (see validation).

coordination_loss_mixed.unit: multiplier on human-pool throughput in the mixed setup
coordination_loss_mixed.rationale: Same as all-human by default; kept separate because people also wait on machines in the mixed line.

new_staff_share.unit: share of roster in first months
new_staff_share.rationale: Staff turnover lever on slide 4. A new store, and churn, mean a share of staff are new.

new_staff_relative_speed.rationale: New staff are slower until trained. With defaults, average speed falls to 0.925x.

min_staff_on_shift.rationale: A counter never runs with fewer people than this. All-machine uses attendant hours instead.

all_machine_attendant_per_open_hour.rationale: Restocking, cleaning, exceptions, customer help. Approved: all-machine is not zero labour.

staffing_flexibility.unit: share of roster gap closed after demand is known
staffing_flexibility.rationale: After opening, rosters move toward real demand; this share of the gap is closed (hiring, part-timers, shift changes). Machines get 0.

labour_cost_per_hour.unit: SGD per hour worked, fully loaded (statutory costs)
labour_cost_per_hour.source: L-mom-pwm, L-mom-ows, L-cpf, L-sdl, L-mom-leave, L-mom-ph
labour_cost_per_hour.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026 (was 14.09). Monthly gross S$2,295 = PWM minimum for a food service counter attendant from 1 Jul 2026 (L-mom-pwm); it binds because the June 2025 market medians are lower (barista S$2,242, counter attendant S$2,279 gross, L-mom-ows; MOM gross wage excludes employer CPF). Plus employer CPF 17% (L-cpf) and SDL 0.25% (L-sdl) = S$2,690.89 a month / 190.67 paid hours (44 h x 52 / 12) = S$14.11 per paid hour; x 286/268 for 18 paid days not worked (7 days annual leave in year 1, L-mom-leave; 11 public holidays, L-mom-ph) on a 5.5-day week (our assumption) = S$15.06 per hour worked. Still a floor: excludes sick leave, bonuses, training, recruitment, uniforms, foreign-worker levies and any 2026 pay above the minimum. Range low = the earlier CPF-only floor (S$14.09); high = USD 20 converted.

machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.unit: SGD per station machine unit per month
machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.represents: Our reading: one semi-automated station unit (for example a dispenser or a cup sealer), amortised with upkeep. Not a robot barista lease; robot prices in machine_tiers.json are per setup. Display text only.
machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.rationale: Amortised purchase plus maintenance, cleaning and consumables. One rate for every station. No Chagee or industry figure in the ledger. Converted from the approved USD 1,500 (range 500-3,000) at fx_sgd_per_usd.

lost_order_cost.rationale: Margin on the cup not sold plus some goodwill. Charged when an order balks because the wait would exceed the target.

capacity_safety_margin.rationale: Same sizing rule for all three setups: capacity for forecast peak x margin. Machines round up to whole units, staff to whole workers.

target_wait_minutes.rationale: A slider, not a claim. An order balks if the wait it would see on arrival exceeds this. The call with Lee Yen mentioned a sub-one-minute fulfilment target, but that is informal and may mean prep time, not total wait; not used or cited.

milk_litres_per_cup.rationale: Milk in a tea latte. Illustrative; not a Chagee recipe figure.

milk_waste_cost_per_litre.rationale: Purchase cost of expired fresh milk. Overseas milk sourcing is unknown (ledger: do not claim), so this is generic.

milk_shelf_life_days.rationale: Generic chilled fresh milk. Stock held beyond this is wasted.

stockout_cost_per_cup.unit: SGD per cup not served for lack of stock
stockout_cost_per_cup.rationale: Set equal to lost_order_cost by default: a missed cup is a missed cup.

opening_stock_days.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 2 rework, changed from 3): slider start = the base forecast over one milk shelf life (provision.milk_shelf_life_days), i.e. the naive 'order the forecast' choice, so the cost-minimising order the calculator marks sits visibly above it. The first order is assumed to cover one shelf life before regular replenishment; stock beyond that window is wasted. The 3 previously approved was the slider start only and was mis-described as 'one shelf life'.

overseas_stores_per_year.rationale: About 200 overseas stores planned for 2026 (L-jiemian). The slide shows it as 'about 200' and as a slider.

saving_per_cup.rationale: Default = mixed vs all-machine cost-per-cup gap at the slide 2 default uncertainty and the default surge. Not hand-set.

waste_avoided.rationale: Default = slide 3 waste-plus-stockout saving from a narrower band. Not hand-set.

business_case._note: Appendix A4 revenue and cost analysis only. Costs of building and running the four gates. Never feeds the cost model in sim/. No sales revenue: there is no price or demand-elasticity assumption, so the benefit side is the modelled avoided cost from the benefit slide.

horizon_years.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Length of the A4 table, matching the five-year horizon of the course examples of a revenue and cost analysis.

opening_year_share.unit: share of a year a store trades in its opening year
opening_year_share.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Mid-year convention: openings spread evenly through the year, so a new store earns half a year of counter saving in its opening year. Openings are held flat at benefit.overseas_stores_per_year every year: L-jiemian covers 2026 only, so we assume no growth.

specialist_day_rate.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Blended rate for data, software and analyst staff, in-house or outsourced. No ledger figure; illustrative. Same structure as the course examples (people x days x rate).

working_days_per_month.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Standard working month, used to turn person-months into person-days.

build_people.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Year 1 build team, one per gate: demand forecast (Predict), ordering calculator (Provision), counter comparison (Counter), review dashboard (Review).

build_months.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Build and pilot in one market before roll-out.

integration_one_time.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Connecting POS sales, app membership sign-ups and supplier order feeds, plus hardware and software set-up. Lump sum, illustrative.

maintenance_people.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Keep the tools running, refresh assumptions, support market teams.

platform_per_store_month.unit: SGD per store in operation per month
platform_per_store_month.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Cloud, licences and dashboards for each store using the gates.

review_days_per_opening.rationale: APPROVED (user, 13 Oct 2026). Gate 4: build the updated scenario from observed inputs and compare it with the original plan.

staffing._note: Staff-optimisation slide only (sim/staffing.js). Never feeds the cost-per-cup model. Reuses existing inputs where they exist: hourly demand shares, cups per day, human seconds per cup with coordination and new-staff speed, the minimum all-human crew, the capacity safety margin as the demand-variability buffer, the target wait, the wage and the opening hype. Excluded from the A2 sensitivity sweep.

max_staff_available.unit: people who can be rostered in one day
max_staff_available.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Labour availability: at most this many shifts in a day (one shift per person). Illustrative; no Chagee roster figure.

shift_min_hours.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Shortest shift a person is rostered for. Illustrative, not a legal minimum.

shift_max_hours.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Longest shift, break included. Illustrative.

break_after_hours.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Shifts longer than this include one break in the middle of the shift. Illustrative house rule, not a statement of Singapore employment law.

break_minutes.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Length of that break, in whole half-hours. The person is off the counter, but the break is counted as paid time (conservative for cost).

service_level_target.unit: share of customers who wait no longer than service.target_wait_minutes
service_level_target.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. Service-level requirement in every hour; the range is the slide slider. The wait limit itself is the existing service.target_wait_minutes.

max_utilisation.rationale: PROPOSED 14 Oct 2026, awaiting user approval. No hour is planned busier than this, so staff are not run flat out even when the wait target would allow it. Illustrative.

monte_carlo_draws.rationale: Enough for a smooth curve at build time; stability is checked across seeds.

base_seed.rationale: Fixed so every build gives the same numbers.

minute_step.rationale: Queue updated once per simulated minute.

live_draws.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Playbook 'Your market' panel: Monte Carlo draws per live verdict in the browser; equal to validation.crossover_stability.seeds. More is steadier but slower.

triggers._note: Added for brief-v2 (approved). Ranges searched by sim breakEven(); not new-store forecasts.

volume_trigger_range_cups_per_day.rationale: Approved for the volume trigger only and labelled on slides 'trigger range, not a new-store forecast'. Lower end = cups_per_store_per_year low (100,000) / open_days_per_year. Cost charts keep the approved 278-833 cups/day (cups_per_store_per_year range).

illustration._note: Slide 5 mechanism illustration only (approved). Dimensionless Week 5 units: speed 1 = one full line per hour. Never feeds the cost model.

worker_speeds.rationale: Week 5 Option 1 defaults (week5/build_opim639_deck.py SIM.option1.speeds), reused read-only.

base_load_share.unit: arrival rate as share of the crew's nominal capacity (sum of speeds)
base_load_share.rationale: Approved: base arrivals at 60% of the crew's capacity, so a surge (surge_multiplier) pushes the line past capacity.

value.matched: station rates = 3 x worker speeds (each station does a third of the work; same total speed as the crew)
value.as_sized: station rates scaled so the line's rate / crew nominal rate = all-machine / mixed peak-hour capacity in sim/ (default surge)

machine_sizing.rationale: Approved toggle: 'matched to the crew' shows the mechanism; 'as sized in our cost model' links to slide 6. The as-sized ratio is read from sim/ peakUtilisation(), not typed.

value.matched: machine block rate = the people part's nominal rate (crew speed / hand share), a balanced mixed line
value.as_sized: machine block rate scaled by mixed machine capacity / mixed peak-hour capacity in sim/ (default surge)

mixed_sizing.rationale: APPROVED (user, after step 4 rework). Added for the combined bucket-brigade slide (user request after step 4): the mixed lane shows the machine stations (stations.mixed_machine_stations) as one fixed-rate block feeding a people brigade that pools the hand steps. The hand share is derived from stations.human_seconds_per_cup, not typed. The as-sized ratio is read from sim/ plan() and peakUtilisation(), not typed. Illustration only; never feeds the cost model.

machine_buffer_capacity.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: a small buffer so an upstream machine blocks when the next one is busy.

run_hours.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: one run of the animation.

surge_window_hours.unit: start and end hour of the surge within a run
surge_window_hours.rationale: APPROVED 9 Oct 2026, illustration only: the surge lasts one hour mid-run so the queue can build and then drain.

validation._note: Fixed before anything is run (addition 4). Changing these after seeing results needs explicit sign-off.

breakeven.rationale: Approved (brief-v2 section 6, as amended). breakEven() scans grid_points evenly over a lever's range with fixed seeds, refines each sign change by bisection until the bracket is narrower than tol_x_share_of_range of the range. Pass if the two setups are within tol_cost at the returned value, OR the bracket is that narrow and the cheaper setup changes across it: a 'step' crossing (staff and machines come in whole units), labelled 'step' on slides. grid_points (13, as the uncertainty sweep) added in step 0.

value.engine: Brigade() read from the ENGINE string in week5/build_opim639_deck.py, not modified
value.pass_rule: pooled throughput (sum of speeds, coordination loss = 1) within +/-3% of Week 5 measured throughput for both speed sets
value.info_only: same comparison at walk = 6 (Week 5 Option 1 default); the gap is reported as a calibration point for coordination_loss, not pass/fail

week5_comparison.rationale: walk = 40 is Week 5's 'near-instant walk back, as the lecture assumes', which is what the pooled formula assumes too. 3% allows for simulation granularity.

cost_per_cup_aggregation.rationale: Fixed before any run. Cost per cup at a given u = (sum over simulated stores of machine + labour + lost-order cost) / (sum of cups served). This is the chain-wide cost per cup, and it matches slide 5 (saving per cup x cups). The alternative, the average of each store's own cost per cup, weights low-demand stores more and is not used for the headline.

peak_utilisation_definition.value: forecast peak-hour arrival rate x surge multiplier, divided by the setup's nominal capacity in that hour, at the base forecast (u = 0, demand = base), before random noise
peak_utilisation_definition.rationale: User check (4): does the fixed-speed mechanism ever bind? Reported for none / moderate / large surge, before the full sweep, alongside the simulated share of orders lost in the peak hours.

crossover_definition.value: smallest u at which mixed cost/cup <= all-machine cost/cup and stays <= for every larger u in the sweep, linearly interpolated between grid points
crossover_definition.rationale: If mixed is cheaper at u = 0: 'no crossover, mixed cheaper everywhere'. If never cheaper: 'no crossover, machines cheaper everywhere'. All-human is plotted and reported but is not part of the headline test.

crossover_stability.rationale: Pass if a crossover exists in at least 18 of 20 seeds and the crossover u differs by at most 10 percentage points across them. If it fails, the slide shows a crossover zone or none, not a single point.

sensitivity.value: one-at-a-time: each parameter with a non-null range set to its low then high value, all others at default; report crossover u (or none) and cost/cup at the slide 2 default u
sensitivity.rationale: Shows which assumptions decide the headline; feeds the 'what could shift the balance' panel and Q&A. No pass/fail.

storyboard._note: Storyboard deck only (storyboard/, sim/counter.js). Never feeds the cost model. Day types reuse surge.surge_multiplier and surge.surge_hours: the multiplier lands on the two busiest hours. In this deck the busier day is one the forecast can see coming (calendar, promo, launch), so the roster can be set for it.

day_type_labels.rationale: Labels for the surge keys. Busy = weekend or holiday; event = launch, collab or promo. Illustrative.

day_type_default.rationale: Printed state of the forecast and counter slides: the day where the roster decision matters.

staff_choices.unit: people on the counter in the peak hour
staff_choices.rationale: People range on the side-by-side counter slides (was 1-4; raised so an all-by-hand counter can be tried above its event-day crew of 4). staffing.max_staff_available is the shift-planning limit and is not used here.

print_minute.unit: minute of the peak hour shown in print
print_minute.rationale: The printed snapshot of the counter animation.

pilot_outlets.rationale: Next-step pilot size, from the review comments in the ideation doc.

split_presets.unit: robot stations per split ('today' = stations.mixed_machine_stations, 'all' = every station)
split_presets.rationale: The splits the GM compares. 'Machines make the drink' follows the team's research: robots do cup and ice, tea and milk, toppings, shake and seal; people tag the order and hand it over. All-by-hand and all-robots are the two bounds.

gm_compare_default.unit: split preset keys, options A and B
gm_compare_default.rationale: Opening and printed state of the GM slide (user request): A human-only, B machine-made drink. Display default only; no result depends on it.

walkaway_target.unit: share of peak-hour orders that walk away
walkaway_target.rationale: The GM's service rule for the split table: the fewest people (from the forecast roster up) and the better sharing rule that keep peak-hour walk-aways at or under this share. Illustrative.

extra_staff_search.unit: people above the forecast roster tried by the split table

price_per_cup.rationale: Honeycombers (Feb 2026) and Eatbook (Aug 2024) in-store sightings; indicative, not a current full menu. The GM's playbook only: revenue of an order not lost.

gross_margin_per_cup.unit: share of price (contribution per avoided order: price minus ingredients and packaging)
gross_margin_per_cup.rationale: Our assumption; Chagee does not disclose; 70% is a team estimate, unsourced. Low 0.50, base 0.60, high 0.70. The GM's playbook only.

busy_days_per_year.rationale: Illustrative definition, to confirm with Chagee: busy days = weekend days (52 x 2). An input on the GM's playbook, not a measured count.

event_days_per_year.rationale: Illustrative definition, to confirm with Chagee: event days = Singapore public holidays. An input on the GM's playbook, not a measured count.

forecast_error_scenarios.unit: share by which the forecast misses the day's cups (negative = too low)
forecast_error_scenarios.rationale: Slide 09 sensitivity only. Scenario steps, not a measured forecast accuracy: Chagee's forecast error is unknown. The roster is set from the wrong forecast; the customers are the day's actual ones.

route_near_travel_min.rationale: Proposal 1, smart pickup routing (slides 05-06). Illustrative scenario for one customer at peak, not live Chagee data. Travel from the customer to the nearer outlet (Suntec City).

route_near_ready_min.rationale: Proposal 1, smart pickup routing (slides 05-06). Illustrative scenario for one customer at peak, not live Chagee data. Time until the drink is ready at the busy nearer outlet.

route_far_travel_min.rationale: Proposal 1, smart pickup routing (slides 05-06). Illustrative scenario for one customer at peak, not live Chagee data. Travel from the customer to the quieter outlet (Raffles City).

route_far_ready_min.rationale: Proposal 1, smart pickup routing (slides 05-06). Illustrative scenario for one customer at peak, not live Chagee data. Time until the drink is ready at the quieter outlet.

route_trigger_wait_min.rationale: Proposal 1, smart pickup routing (slide 06). Illustrative trigger: the agent acts when a store's wait is, or is about to go, above this. Not Chagee data.

p2_overtime_hours_saved.rationale: Proposal 2, AI-assisted staffing (appendix financial case). Illustrative monthly zone case, not Chagee data. Paid overtime hours avoided across the pilot zone.

p2_system_cost_month.rationale: Proposal 2, AI-assisted staffing (appendix financial case). Illustrative monthly zone case, not Chagee data. Recurring system and support cost for the zone.

sitepick._note: Slide 13 new-store forecast only (sim/sitepick.js). SYNTHETIC app demand on the team's Singapore map (sim/sg_geo.json, image pixels). Never feeds the cost model. Hub positions are the map's place labels; weights are illustrative, not population data.

km_per_px.rationale: The island spans about 1,420 px on the map and roughly 47 km west to east. The map is not to scale, so distances are approximate.

hubs.rationale: Where app sessions concentrate: the map's place labels as town centres. Tengah and Choa Chu Kang are included with no outlet nearby, as new or growing towns. Illustrative.

hub_spread_km.unit: km, standard deviation around a hub
hub_spread_km.rationale: Size of a town's demand area.

events.unit: synthetic app-intent dots on the map
events.rationale: Each dot stands for a fixed number of app sessions a day; the number is set by calibration (see calibration_cups_per_outlet).

background_share.unit: share of dots spread evenly over land

mall_share.unit: share of dots placed around the outlets' malls
mall_share.rationale: Outlets sit in malls with their own footfall, so part of app intent is centred on each outlet (equal for every outlet). Without it, a store opened beside an outlet barely touched that outlet's sales.

mall_spread_km.unit: km, standard deviation around an outlet

walk_km.unit: km a customer will walk to collect
walk_km.rationale: Slider. A session whose nearest outlet is further than this is logged as a 'no store nearby' search; it also sets the distance decay (decay_share). Tuned with decay_share, hub_spread_km and mall_share so a bit under half of app intent is unmet, the middle 80% of outlets sell roughly 300 to 870 cups a day, and a store opened beside an outlet takes most from that outlet.

decay_share.unit: distance decay length as a share of walk_km
decay_share.rationale: Pull of a store = exp(-(distance / L)^2 / 2), L = walk_km x decay_share: bell-shaped, so a store at the walking limit pulls about 61% of one next door and almost nothing beyond 3 L. (A slower exponential decay was tried first; it spread a new store's cannibalisation over outlets several km away, which is not credible.)

outside_option.unit: pull of not buying, against a store next door (= 1)
outside_option.rationale: Proximity split (Huff-style): share bought at store j = pull_j / (outside + sum of pulls). A session next to one store converts 1 / 1.3, about 77%.

dbscan_eps_km.rationale: Slider. DBSCAN neighbourhood radius for 'no store nearby' searches.

dbscan_min_points.unit: dots within eps to form a cluster core

calibration_cups_per_outlet.rationale: The dot weight is set so the average existing outlet sells the deck's cups per day. A pin's forecast is then in the same units.

candidates_shown.rationale: Top clusters by net new cups.

verdict.unit: share of the new store's cups that are new to Chagee
verdict.rationale: The GM's read of a pin: at or above strong_new_share it is a strong site (it mostly adds cups); below weak_new_share it mostly moves cups from existing outlets; in between, mixed. Illustrative cut-offs.

toy_demo.unit: toy points in a 600 x 330 box
toy_demo.rationale: Explainer only: a small made-up point set for the 'How it works' walkthrough on slide 13 and the appendix figure, so each DBSCAN step is visible. Not used by any forecast.

site_ext._note: The four-scores and pin-to-profit slides only (things to consider: Jin's site-selection framework, I-team-site-framework). Singapore only. Illustrative, synthetic data, not Chagee data. Never feeds the benefit, the cost model or any decision check. Cups a day, price and margin are NOT here: they are the benefit slide's inputs (store.cups_per_store_per_year, storyboard.price_per_cup, storyboard.gross_margin_per_cup), and the build fails if slide 11 shows other values.

scores.rationale: Hand-set. The site engine (sim/sitepick.js) has no residents, workers, transit tap-ins, delivery-app orders or competitor locations, so it cannot produce these three scores. In production a supervised model would score them from the attributes. The cannibalisation factor is not here: it is computed by the engine.

score_weights.unit: weight in the site score, sums to 1
score_weights.rationale: Hand-set weights for the site score out of 100. Cannibalisation is not in the score; it is deducted in the profit.

ring_km.rationale: Radius for 'Chagee outlets within' a pin (Jin's attribute). Display and the contrast pin's selection only.

competition_radius_m.rationale: Radius for competing bubble-tea and cafe outlets (Jin's attribute). Display only.

residents_radius_km.rationale: Radius for residents and workers (Jin's attribute). Display only.

rent_per_month.rationale: Illustrative mall-unit rent. No Chagee or market rent figure in the ledger.

utilities_per_month.rationale: Illustrative electricity, water and service charges. No ledger figure.

delivery_share_of_cups.unit: share of the outlet's cups sold through third-party delivery apps
delivery_share_of_cups.rationale: Illustrative. All Chagee delivery is via third-party apps (I-chagee-contact); the share is not public.

delivery_commission_share.unit: share of a delivery order's price paid to the platform
delivery_commission_share.rationale: Illustrative platform commission. No ledger figure; Chagee's terms are not public.

setup_cost.unit: SGD per new outlet, one-off (fit-out, equipment, deposits, opening)
setup_cost.rationale: Illustrative. Payback = set-up cost / net monthly profit to Chagee.

lookalike_labels.rationale: Anonymised display labels for look-alike outlets on the pin-to-profit slide. Not real outlets; the look-alike step is not run here.

recommendation_rule.value: open if net monthly profit to Chagee is positive at the low end of the cups-a-day range; pilot if positive at the default but not at the low end; skip if not positive at the default
recommendation_rule.rationale: Derives the pin-to-profit slide's recommendation from the computed numbers.

model.unit: ridge penalty on standardised features; delivery radius km; cap on distance to the nearest outlet km
model.rationale: The supervised site model (sim/sitemodel.js): ridge regression trained on the slide 13 engine's synthetic outlet cups a day, tested by leave-one-out. A small penalty keeps the fit stable with few outlets. Illustrative; not trained on Chagee data.

new_market_inputs.unit: feature keys a market with no Chagee history would have (preset on the supervised site model)
new_market_inputs.rationale: Our assumption: population and town-centre distance exist anywhere; delivery-area demand depends on platform data (to confirm); app searches and the outlet network do not exist before Chagee opens.

new_city.unit: a hypothetical city: km, town centres and weights; grid spacing km; stores to place (default and maximum)
new_city.rationale: The supervised site model's proxy for a new market: a made-up city, not a real place. Its population dots are generated at Singapore's synthetic density (same dots per unit of town weight and same even background per km2 as the slide 13 events), so the model's inputs mean the same thing in both. With real data, a census population grid and real town centres replace it.

_note.rationale: Australia worked example, kept separate from every other section: nothing here feeds the main story (slides 01 to 15) or the benefit and nothing in them is changed. Every Australian input is a scenario assumption; no Australian data has been retrieved for this deck. Archetype areas stand in for real suburbs until Census and market data are pulled.

currency.rationale: Every money figure on the new-market slides and the new-market pilot slide is in Australian dollars (A$). No exchange rate is applied to any Singapore figure.

market_status.value: no local Chagee operating history (assumed for this worked example)
market_status.rationale: Treated as a market with no Chagee outlet, app history or delivery history in the catchments; to confirm before use.

areas.unit: archetype candidate areas in one Australian state capital; people within 1 km (thousands), income index (city = 100), transit index (0-1), bubble-tea and cafe competitors within 500 m, rent A$ a month for one counter outlet; x, y schematic km
areas.rationale: Scenario assumptions, not observations: illustrative archetypes chosen to differ on every feature so the ranking has something to rank. Replace with real suburbs and the sourced values listed in features.planned_source before any decision.

value.label: Residents within 1 km
value.proxy_for: walk-in demand from people living nearby
value.planned_source: national census, usual residents by small area

value.label: Tertiary students within 1 km
value.planned_source: university and TAFE enrolment by campus

value.label: Household income index
value.proxy_for: willingness to pay for a premium tea

value.label: Transit access
value.planned_source: public-transport timetable data, services per hour at the nearest stops

value.label: Competitors within 500 m
value.proxy_for: rival bubble-tea and cafe supply (lowers the score)
value.planned_source: business listings or a map-places count

value.label: Rent, A$ a month
value.planned_source: retail lease listings or an agent quote

features.unit: candidate-area features: key, label, what it stands in for, where a real value would come from, direction in the score (+1 raises, -1 lowers)
features.rationale: Only features a market with no Chagee history can measure. planned_source names the kind of public data; none of it has been retrieved, so every value is a scenario assumption on the slides.

value.label: Chagee app searches nearby
value.why: needs Chagee app users in the market

value.label: Delivery orders from the area
value.why: needs Chagee on the local delivery platforms

value.label: Distance to the nearest Chagee outlet
Sales of existing Chagee outlets nearby

excluded.unit: features left out of the profile
excluded.rationale: They need existing Chagee activity. Missing is unknown, not zero: they are left out, never set to zero, so no area is marked down for a gap every area shares.

weights.unit: relative weight per feature in the suitability score (0-2)
weights.rationale: Our judgement, illustrative. The new-market ranking slide lets you move each; the sensitivity check re-ranks with each weight set to zero and doubled.

sensitivity.unit: multipliers applied to one weight at a time
sensitivity.rationale: One-at-a-time sensitivity: each weight times zero (dropped) and times two; the rank range is reported per area.

demand_scenarios.unit: cups a day: low, base, high
demand_scenarios.rationale: Placeholder scale only: the Singapore per-outlet volume assumption (itself an assumption, not Chagee data) reused for every Australian area. The score does not set cups: without a calibration from real outlets, every area faces the same range.

forecast_error.unit: share by which the pre-opening forecast misses realised cups a day
forecast_error.rationale: Scenario assumption: before opening, the forecast cannot know actual demand. Under-forecast, exact, over-forecast.

wage_per_hour.unit: AUD per hour worked, fully loaded
wage_per_hour.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced. Replace with the applicable award rate plus on-costs before use.

machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.unit: AUD per station machine unit per month
machine_cost_per_unit_per_month.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced; the Singapore figure is also an assumption and no exchange rate is applied.

price_per_cup.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced. Check menu prices in the pilot city.

setups.rationale: Human-only against machine-made drink, as on slide 11; same station speeds and staffing rule (sim/counter.js).

cannibalisation.unit: for a second opening: share of a new outlet's cups taken from the pilot, falling linearly to zero at overlap_km
cannibalisation.rationale: Scenario assumption. Zero for the first opening: no Chagee outlet is in any catchment.

scan.unit: realised cups a day as multiples of the base scenario
scan.rationale: Range of the contribution chart on the new-market setup slide.

trigger_weeks.unit: consecutive weeks a pilot signal must hold before acting

day_mix.unit: busy and event days a year; the rest of store.open_days_per_year are normal days
day_mix.rationale: Scenario assumption for the Australian pilot: busy days = weekend days; event days = a guess at local public holidays and events, not counted. Weights the year-average contribution on the new-market setup slide.

_note.rationale: Five-year projection of the same new outlet at two sites (slide 13): beside the existing outlet nearest the selected site, without AI, and the selected site, with AI-assisted site selection. Same opening date, equipment and staffing rule in both, so only the site differs. Illustrative scenarios, not demonstrated causal gains from AI. Nothing here feeds the benefit or any other slide.

years.rationale: Projection horizon; both scenarios open on the same date.

ramp_up.unit: share of steady-state cups in each year from opening
ramp_up.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced: the first year runs below steady state while the outlet becomes known. Same in both scenarios. demand.opening_hype_multiplier is opening-week hype, a different effect, and is not used here.

demand_growth.unit: share a year, applied to both scenarios' cups from year two
demand_growth.rationale: Default no growth: no existing assumption justifies one (benefit.overseas_stores_per_year is held flat for the same reason). Slider for sensitivity.

cost_inflation.unit: share a year, applied to wage, rent, utilities, maintenance, machine and recurring AI costs from year two
cost_inflation.rationale: Default none; price is held flat too, so the default projection is in today's dollars. Slider for sensitivity.

store_maintenance_per_month.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced: premises and non-machine repairs. Machine maintenance is already inside costs.machine_cost_per_unit_per_month, so it is not counted again.

ai_implementation_cost.unit: SGD one-off: building the site-selection analysis on Chagee's app logs
ai_implementation_cost.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced. Treated as an investment at opening (in the payback), not an operating cost.

ai_recurring_per_year.unit: SGD a year: data pipeline, cloud and analyst time to rerun it
ai_recurring_per_year.rationale: Scenario assumption, not sourced. An operating cost in the AI scenario only.

ai_cost_share_to_outlet.unit: share of the AI costs charged to this one outlet
ai_cost_share_to_outlet.rationale: Conservative default: the whole AI cost is charged to this outlet. A lower share spreads it over other openings; we assume no number of openings (Chagee's plan is confidential).

volume_scenarios.unit: multipliers on both sites' cups: low, base, high
volume_scenarios.rationale: Scenario range from our per-outlet volume range (an assumption), applied to the sold and the displaced cups alike. Not a statistical confidence interval.

_note.rationale: Members: squad tiers. An analytics model (Topic 8 network effects), not AI. Every parameter is illustrative, not Chagee data; the model shows direction and what to pilot, not effect sizes. Nothing here feeds the benefit or any other slide.

value.text: we cannot accurately predict the rate or range of consumers who will join our membership program
value.source: Chagee Form 20-F, FY 2025, Item 3.D, risk factors
value.excerpt: We have limited experience operating our membership program and we cannot accurately predict the rate or range of consumers who will join our membership program.

value.text: we may not be able to use our membership program to deepen our understanding of our target consumers
value.source: Chagee Form 20-F, FY 2025, Item 3.D, same risk factor
value.excerpt: In addition, we may not be able to use our membership program to deepen our understanding of our target consumers.

value.text: The value z′ is the hump the firm must get over in order to succeed.
value.excerpt: downward pressure downward pressure upward pressure unstable equilibrium (critical point / tipping point) stable equilibrium The value z′ is the hump the firm must get over in order to succeed.

quotes.unit: verbatim quotes on slide 05, each with the source text it was checked against (excerpt)
quotes.rationale: Tests require each quote to be an exact substring of its excerpt. Dropped: the Q1 2026 'active members' quote, which we could not check against a source we hold.

squad_size.rationale: Our proposal, a design choice, not a Chagee feature claim.

scenarios.unit: p = effort cost of tiering up (0-1); k = how much others using the app is worth (f(z) = k z)
scenarios.rationale: Illustrative, not Chagee data. Squads raise k; a launch incentive lowers p.

expected_table.unit: z' and z'' to the nearest percentage point; null = no positive equilibrium
expected_table.rationale: The user's expected values. The build fails if the computed table differs.

rounds.unit: adoption rounds shown in the animation

network.unit: network check: customers, average friends each (seeded random graph), seeded runs, rounds cap, precision of the starting share, final share above which a run has not collapsed
network.rationale: Assumption: eight friends each, a squad plus a few more. The closed form assumes everyone sees the whole population's share; a friend group sees a noisy sample of it.

group_credit_share.unit: share of the price credited on each group order
group_credit_share.rationale: New input, assumption, not Chagee data.

extra_orders_per_member_month.unit: extra orders a squad member places a month because of squads
extra_orders_per_member_month.rationale: New input, assumption, not Chagee data.

base_group_orders_per_member_month.unit: group orders a squad member would place a month anyway, which also earn the credit
base_group_orders_per_member_month.rationale: Invented for the break-even (the credit is paid on orders that would have happened anyway); assumption, not Chagee data.

example_interest.unit: interest r of the one customer drawn on slide 05, steps one and two
example_interest.rationale: Display only: a middling customer, to separate one customer's benefit from the equilibrium curve.

Mei.why: you often pick floral teas at lunch and rated an oolong highly

Jun.why: you switched to less sugar in your last few orders

Aisha.why: you liked jasmine teas when ordering for yourself

Ravi.why: close to your usual, with the sugar level you picked last week

app_rules.unit: illustrative rules and copy for the M2 prototype: points for your own drink, points every member gets for each drink in a group order, the member's points now and for the next tier, tier names, personas; each persona's usual drink, a suggested alternative with its reason, and gift options for the recipient
app_rules.rationale: Our illustrative rules for the proposed experience, used consistently on slide 06. Not Chagee's membership rules, which are to confirm. The group-order credit is members.group_credit_share. Preferences and suggestions are illustrative data, not learned from anyone. Recalling the last order is the baseline; the proposed AI part ranks alternatives from each member's own choices, acceptances and dismissals. No real messages, purchases or accounts.

ai_cost_per_member_month.unit: S$ per participating member a month
ai_cost_per_member_month.rationale: Illustrative placeholder, not sourced: the running cost of personalised suggestions per participating member, allocated. Replace with a quoted cost before any decision. Used only on slide 08 to show what personalisation must add on top of squads.

_note.rationale: A synthetic demonstration of the mechanics only: one outlet's peak half-hour pickup window, with squad signals generated by our assumptions. The enhanced forecast can only help to the extent we assume the signals carry information, so this shows how the forecast would work, not measured accuracy. Nothing here feeds any other slide.

window_minutes.rationale: The window is the peak hour's first half (store.hourly_demand_share), so its calendar baseline is the deck's own volume: cups a day x the peak hour's share / 2.

lead_minutes.unit: minutes before the window that the playback starts

social_share.unit: share of the window's cups that come through squad group orders and gifts, on average
social_share.rationale: Hypothesis to test; zero means no squad signals, and the enhanced forecast then equals the baseline.

invites_per_basket.unit: people invited to a group basket, on average (squad size 2 to 6)

member_conversion.unit: share of invited members who confirm a drink
member_conversion.rationale: Illustrative; the forecast does not know it and estimates it from synthetic history.

confirm_delay_minutes.unit: average minutes from a basket opening to a member confirming

gifts_per_window.unit: gifts sent for this window, on average, at the default squad share (scales with the squad share)

gift_redeem_share.unit: share of gifts redeemed for this window
gift_redeem_share.rationale: Illustrative; an unredeemed gift is never counted as a drink.

gift_redeem_delay_minutes.unit: average minutes from sending a gift to its redemption

day_shock_sd.unit: spread of the day's demand around the calendar baseline (both walk-in and squad cups move with it)
day_shock_sd.rationale: Illustrative: why the calendar baseline misses on any one day.

history_windows.unit: past synthetic windows the enhanced forecast learns its conversion and late-arrival rates from
history_windows.rationale: Synthetic history, same generator, different seeds.

eval_windows.unit: synthetic windows used to compare the two forecasts (appendix)

eval_leads.unit: minutes before the window at which the forecasts are compared

day_picks.unit: actual cups against the calendar baseline for the three example days on the slide (quiet, typical, busy)
day_picks.rationale: Display: the example days are the seeds whose actual cups, as a share of the baseline, are closest to these.

success_pick.unit: actual cups against the calendar baseline for the fourth example day on slide 07 (squad rush)
success_pick.rationale: Display: a success case chosen by rule, not by hand. Among the same 300 synthetic windows, only those where the squad forecast is closer than the history-only forecast at the slide's default minute; of those, the one whose actual cups are closest to this share of the baseline. The slide also states the share of all windows where the squad forecast was closer, so the case is not presented as typical of every day.

drink_mix.unit: share of cups by drink, for predicted cups not yet chosen
drink_mix.rationale: Illustrative generic drinks, not Chagee's menu or sales mix.

_note.value: Five-year financial model of proposals 1-3 (Financial impact slide, appendix table, chagee_financial_model.xlsx)
_note.rationale: Incremental to today's operations only: the extra cups, savings and costs the three proposals cause. Base volumes, price, margin, wage and machine cost reuse the deck's existing assumptions. Every new input below is illustrative, not Chagee data.

years.rationale: 2026 sets up the project team; pilots start January 2027 (execution plan); scale from 2028.

gross_margin.source: Chagee's reported corporate gross margin, about 54% (figure provided by the team; check against Chagee's latest annual report before submission)
gross_margin.rationale: Used for every gross-profit line in the financial model: extra sales from the proposals and the Singapore forecast.

organic_growth.unit: growth in cups per outlet per year
organic_growth.rationale: Illustrative same-store growth in cups, without the proposals. Applied to existing and new outlets.

cups_per_outlet.unit: cups per outlet per year, stabilised
cups_per_outlet.source: Team-provided: a stabilised Chagee outlet in Singapore averages about 230,000 to 250,000+ cups a year; midpoint used
cups_per_outlet.rationale: Used for the financial model and the Singapore forecast. The earlier counter simulations keep their own figure.

wage_inflation.unit: growth in the hourly wage per year
wage_inflation.rationale: Illustrative wage inflation, applied to outlet staff costs and to the value of staff hours saved. Rent held flat.

crew_on_shift.unit: staff on shift, average across the open day
crew_on_shift.rationale: Illustrative. More at the peak, fewer when quiet. Used only for the Singapore forecast's labour line.

p1_coverage.unit: share of outlets covered in the year
p1_coverage.rationale: Proposal 1: one-zone test from January 2027, expanding zone by zone; every outlet from July 2027 (2H2027).

p2_coverage.unit: share of outlets covered in the year
p2_coverage.rationale: Proposal 2: forecasts from February, one-zone test April-May, launch June; every outlet from July 2027 (2H2027).

effectiveness.rationale: The shared model keeps learning: about two-thirds of the full effect in 2027, near full by 2029.

new_stores.unit: new outlets opened in the year
new_stores.rationale: Two outlets chosen with the site model in 2027 (execution plan), then one a year: Singapore is already quite saturated. Each opens mid-year. Their normal sales join the baseline; only the extra sales from a better site count towards Proposal 3.

p1_lost_share.unit: share of cups lost at peak (walk-aways, crowding)
p1_lost_share.rationale: Illustrative. Cups customers would have bought but did not, because of queues.

p1_recovery_share.unit: share of lost cups recovered by redirection
p1_recovery_share.rationale: Illustrative. Customers who switch outlet or delivery channel instead of leaving.

p1_redirect_share.unit: share of all orders redirected to another outlet
p1_redirect_share.rationale: Illustrative. Perks go to every redirected order, not only to customers who would otherwise have walked away, so redirected orders exceed recovered cups.

p1_voucher_share.unit: share of redirected orders given a switch perk
p1_voucher_share.rationale: Illustrative. Perks only while an outlet is swamped; some customers switch without one.

p1_voucher_cost.rationale: Illustrative average cost of a voucher or carrier bag.

p2_extra_cup_share.unit: share of cups added at the peak
p2_extra_cup_share.rationale: Illustrative. Staff and machines ready for busy days.

p2_idle_hours_week.unit: paid idle hours avoided per outlet per week
p2_idle_hours_week.rationale: Illustrative. Rosters flex down on quiet days.

p2_waste_share.unit: fresh stock written off, share of revenue
p2_waste_share.rationale: Illustrative. Perishables prepped but not sold.

p2_waste_cut.rationale: Illustrative. Fresh prep matched to each week's demand.

p2_machines_saved.unit: net machine units avoided per outlet
p2_machines_saved.rationale: Illustrative. Some outlets run one fewer, a few add one; the net is small.

p3_uplift.unit: extra net-new cups at an AI-chosen site vs a conventional pick
p3_uplift.rationale: Illustrative. Only the uplift is attributed to the site model, not the new outlet's whole revenue.

team_months.unit: months of our project team (project manager and AI engineer) in the year
team_months.rationale: Design and plan from October 2026; build, pilot and launch through 2027. From 2028 a smaller run team takes over.

platform_build.rationale: Illustrative, lean set-up: the dashboard and assistant run on off-the-shelf BI and AI services, configured rather than custom-built; external developers only add the app pop-up and the delivery-app link. Forecasts and the site model are built by our AI engineer, already costed in the project team.

data_setup.rationale: Illustrative. Connecting the POS, app, delivery and stock data to one cloud warehouse, using standard connectors.

security_review.rationale: Illustrative. Security testing and a PDPA review before customer data drives app pop-ups.

training_per_outlet.rationale: Cross-training is delivered by existing zone and store managers during normal shifts: no incremental cost.

training_outlets.rationale: All 44 outlets plus the two new ones as Proposals 1 and 2 roll out in 2027; each later new outlet after that.

run_team_year.unit: SGD a year at full scale
run_team_year.rationale: AI engineer full-time (12 x S$14k) and project manager half-time (12 x S$6k), at the project team's rates, to run and improve the platform.

cloud_year.unit: SGD a year at full scale
cloud_year.rationale: Illustrative: cloud compute, data warehouse and AI services for about 50 outlets, plus dashboard licences for managers and assistant usage.

maintenance_share.unit: share of the platform build, per year
maintenance_share.rationale: Typical yearly upkeep of externally built software: fixes, app-store and delivery-app API changes. From launch.

chagee_time_year.rationale: Chagee's supply chain, zone and store managers work on the project as part of their existing roles: no incremental cost. Kept as a row so the time is visible.

build_share.unit: share of the one-off build spent in the year
build_share.rationale: Platform and data set-up are built and paid for during the 2027 pilots.

cloud_share.unit: share of a full year of cloud costs
cloud_share.rationale: Pilot zones in 1H2027, every outlet from 2H2027; full from 2028.

run_share.unit: share of a full year of the run team
run_share.rationale: From 2028 a smaller run team replaces the project team.
